status.label: Reproduce repeated Spanish-layout punctuation remaps
status.detail: Holding Ctrl while alternating the mapped dot/comma shortcuts reportedly stops producing the intended angle brackets after a few repetitions.

judgment.rationale: The report lists PowerToys 0.87.1, Windows 10, and a Spanish-Mexico setup, with two exact mappings: Ctrl+dot to the '<' key and Ctrl+comma to Shift+'<'. The reporter says alternating the source keys while holding Ctrl initially emits the intended angle-bracket sequence, then falls back to literal punctuation after about three outputs. It occurs in any text input, with Notepad and Firefox named. No comments or current-version confirmation are present.
evidence: The report includes the exact two shortcut mappings and the sequence of alternating dot/comma while Ctrl remains held.
The reporter observes the first few angle brackets and then literal dots/commas.
The report lists Spanish-Mexico and PowerToys 0.87.1; Notepad and Firefox are named test applications.
The issue is open and unassigned with no comments; no linked fix was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the exact repeated-input sequence on current stable with the Spanish-Mexico layout and inspect whether the original Ctrl shortcut events leak after repeated remap dispatch.

fix_assessment.rationale: If current builds reproduce the fallback, the repeated shortcut handling may lose a modifier or remap state after several injected outputs. The layout and repeated-input event path need confirmation before selecting an implementation.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep repeated punctuation shortcut remaps active
proposed_fixes.root_cause: When Ctrl remains held across alternating punctuation shortcut mappings, Keyboard Manager may stop consuming the source events or lose modifier state after repeated injected output. The report does not include a current build or event trace.
plan: Reproduce the two mappings on current stable with Spanish-Mexico active.
Compare one-shot presses with rapid and slow alternation while Ctrl remains held.
Inspect modifier and key-up state around the third remapped output and identify where literal source punctuation resumes.
Correct the confirmed state transition and add a regression test for repeated modifier-held shortcut mappings.
verification: Verify repeated Ctrl+dot/Ctrl+comma presses continue producing the intended angle brackets.
Verify Ctrl and punctuation keys are released correctly after each mapped output.
Verify ordinary punctuation and other Spanish-layout shortcuts remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The exact sequence and failure threshold are described, but current behavior and the event-state transition are unverified.
